Recursion is a programming technique where a function solves a problem by calling itself with a smaller piece of the same problem. Each call does a little work and then hands the rest off to another call of itself, until the problem becomes so small that the function just returns an answer directly—this simple case is called the base case. For example, to compute the factorial of n, you multiply n by the factorial of n−1, and when n reaches 1, you just return 1. The key is making sure every recursive call moves closer to the base case, otherwise the function will call itself forever and crash.
